newsitem.title: USA: U.S. safety official prods FAA on TWA crash steps.
newsitem.headline: U.S. safety official prods FAA on TWA crash steps.

text.p: A top safety official complained on Tuesday that the Federal Aviation Administration had failed to act on urgent recommendations meant to prevent explosions like the one that brought down TWA Flight 800.
Almost seven months after the National Transportation Safety Board made its proposals, the FAA was still far from implementing them, NTSB chairman James Hall said in a letter to the FAA.

On Dec. 13, 1996, the NTSB recommended measures to prevent the build-up of explosive fuel-air mixtures in airline fuel tanks, responding to the July 17, 1996, TWA disaster, which investigators believe may have been caused by an explosion in the center fuel tank.
The Paris-bound Boeing 747 operated by Trans World Airlines exploded shortly after takeoff from New York's Kennedy airport, killing all 230 people aboard.
The FAA has called for public comment on the recommendations, and in a letter to the NTSB last Friday, it said there was a need for more research into the cause of the explosion.
The letter did not suggest the FAA was taking any immediate action.
"Your letter makes clear that our differences are not likely to be resolved in the near future," Hall told FAA Acting Administrator Barry Valentine in his reply on Tuesday.
Hall repeated his proposal that "urgent consideration be given to immediate operational measures that could reduce the risks identified in the flight 800 tragedy."
